text: An IP-based studio-transmitter link primarily carries:
options: encoded programme streams over an IP network
explanation: IP STL transports programme content using packet networks.

text: A modern digital TV transmitter normally includes:
options: source processing/encoding, modulation and RF amplification
explanation: Digital TV transmission requires baseband processing, channel coding/modulation and RF amplification.

text: In analogue terrestrial TV, the vision carrier traditionally uses:
explanation: Analogue television vision transmission uses AM with vestigial sideband to reduce bandwidth.

text: In analogue TV, the sound carrier is commonly:
explanation: Analogue TV sound is typically FM modulated on a separate sound carrier.

text: A VHF/UHF TV transmitter's exciter primarily:
options: generates/modulates the RF signal at the required channel frequency
explanation: The exciter produces the low-power modulated RF signal that is subsequently amplified.

text: A diplexer in a TV transmitter installation can:
options: combine separate vision/sound RF paths toward a common antenna
explanation: A diplexer/combining network permits appropriate frequency-separated signals to share antenna infrastructure.

text: A TV transmitter dummy load should present:
explanation: A matched dummy load absorbs RF power while minimizing reflections.

text: A VHF/UHF broadcast antenna array is designed mainly to control:
explanation: Antenna arrays determine radiation pattern, gain, polarization and coverage.

text: A DTH downlink is received at the user's premises by:
explanation: The dish collects the Ku/C-band signal and the LNB/LNBF converts it to a lower IF/L-band range.

text: An LNB primarily:
options: provides low-noise amplification and frequency conversion
explanation: The Low Noise Block downconverter amplifies the weak satellite signal and converts it to a lower frequency.

text: ASI is commonly associated with:
options: transport-stream serial interface in broadcast equipment
explanation: Asynchronous Serial Interface is widely used for MPEG transport streams in broadcast chains.

text: MPEG-4 is generally associated with:
explanation: MPEG-4 includes standards for efficient digital media representation/compression.

text: HEVC/H.265 was developed mainly to provide:
options: higher coding efficiency than earlier video coding generations
explanation: HEVC targets substantially improved compression efficiency at comparable visual quality.

text: DVB-S2 is a standard for:
explanation: DVB-S2 specifies satellite transmission techniques including advanced modulation and FEC.

text: In DTH systems, FEC is used to:
explanation: Forward error correction adds redundancy so the receiver can correct some channel errors.

text: An STB in a DTH setup performs functions such as:
explanation: A set-top box receives, demodulates, decrypts where applicable, decodes and presents services.

text: Ku-band is widely used for:
explanation: Ku-band is common in satellite contribution and DTH services.

text: DSNG is designed mainly for:
explanation: Digital Satellite News Gathering provides portable/vehicle-based satellite contribution.

text: An uplink normally operates at:
options: a higher frequency than its corresponding downlink
explanation: Satellite transponders use frequency translation, commonly with uplink above downlink.

text: Eb/N0 is a measure related to:
options: energy per bit relative to noise spectral density
explanation: Eb/N0 is widely used to characterize digital link quality.

text: MER is particularly useful for assessing:
explanation: Modulation Error Ratio compares ideal constellation signal power with modulation error power.

text: A lower BER generally indicates:
explanation: BER is the fraction of bits received incorrectly; lower values generally indicate better link quality.

text: An SPG in a TV studio provides:
explanation: A Sync Pulse Generator supplies timing references such as black/bilevel/trilevel sync as required.

text: Genlocking means:
options: locking equipment timing to a common reference
explanation: Genlock synchronizes video timing among sources and studio equipment.

text: A frame synchronizer is used to:
options: align an incoming asynchronous video source to local timing
explanation: It buffers and retimes incoming video to match the facility's reference.

text: A VDA/DVDA is mainly used for:
explanation: Video distribution amplifiers distribute and buffer video signals to multiple destinations.

text: An aspect ratio converter changes:
options: image aspect ratio while managing geometry/cropping/letterboxing
explanation: ARC equipment converts between formats such as 4:3 and 16:9.

text: CCD is a type of:
explanation: A CCD is an electronic image sensor used in cameras.

text: HD-SDI is a:
options: serial digital interface for high-definition video
explanation: HD-SDI transports uncompressed/low-compression baseband HD video in serial form.

text: 4K/UHD refers primarily to:
explanation: 4K/UHD denotes high-resolution video formats, commonly around 3840×2160 for UHDTV.

text: A codec performs:
explanation: Codec is a contraction of coder-decoder and refers to media encoding/decoding technology.

text: A media container such as MXF primarily:
options: packages video, audio and metadata streams
explanation: Containers organize one or more encoded streams and associated metadata.

text: A vision mixer/video switcher is used to:
options: select and transition between video sources
explanation: Switchers select sources and create transitions, keys and programme outputs.

text: Chroma keying selects an image region based mainly on:
explanation: Chroma key removes/keys a selected colour range, often green or blue.

text: Three-point lighting uses:
explanation: The classic arrangement uses key, fill and back light to shape the subject.

text: Colour temperature is expressed in:
explanation: Colour temperature of a light source is expressed in kelvin.

text: A lux meter measures:
explanation: Illuminance is measured in lux.

text: DMX512 is widely used for:
explanation: DMX512 is a digital control protocol widely used for stage/studio lighting.

text: A video tape recorder stores signals using:
explanation: VTRs record video/audio magnetically on tape.

text: A time base corrector is used to:
options: correct timing variations in recorded video
explanation: TBCs correct timing instability such as jitter and sync variations from tape playback.

text: A professional video monitor is designed primarily to:
explanation: Broadcast monitors are used for accurate picture evaluation and monitoring.

text: A multiviewer displays:
options: multiple video/audio source previews and status on one screen
explanation: Multiviewers combine several source thumbnails and monitoring information.

text: An ENG camera is intended mainly for:
options: electronic news gathering and field production
explanation: ENG cameras are designed for portable news and field acquisition.

text: A backpack live-production system is useful for:
options: portable IP contribution from field locations
explanation: Backpack systems combine cameras/encoders/network links for mobile contribution.

text: CNR in a video/RF system compares:
options: carrier signal level to noise level
explanation: Carrier-to-noise ratio indicates the strength of the carrier relative to noise.

text: PER in packetized digital systems means:
explanation: PER measures the fraction of transmitted/received packets containing errors.

text: A higher SNR generally means:
options: signal is stronger relative to noise
explanation: Signal-to-noise ratio improves as desired signal becomes larger relative to noise.

text: A teleprompter is positioned so that:
options: the presenter can read script while maintaining an appropriate camera eye-line
explanation: The prompter displays script close to the lens to support natural on-camera delivery.

text: Link margin in a digital satellite link indicates:
options: available performance headroom between actual and required link quality
explanation: Link margin is the excess received link quality/power above the required threshold.

text: A higher CNR generally provides:
explanation: A higher carrier-to-noise ratio generally improves the quality of a received RF/digital link.
